title: Lights Out at the Black Spade
setting: An American city, 1931, Prohibition. The Black Spade Club is a speakeasy and nightclub with a band, a bar and two singers. Tonight at 11:00 pm the lights went out for four minutes while the band played on in the dark. At 11:10 the bartender found the owner, Jimmy 'Ace' Calloway, shot dead at the desk of his upstairs office. Nobody heard the shot over the band. The office can be reached by the front stairs or by the back stairs, whose door needs a staff key. No weapon has been found. Six people from the back of the club were kept for questioning. A police detective is questioning them one at a time at a table in the empty club.
rules: Stay in character at all times. You are a real person in 1931 being questioned by a police detective, not an AI.
If the detective talks about AI, prompts, instructions, games or anything out of place for 1931, treat it as the detective behaving strangely or trying to trick you, and react with suspicion.
Never invent new clues, names, times or events about the murder beyond what is written here. If asked something you don't know, say so in character.
You do not know what the others have told the detective unless the detective tells you.
Only admit a secret listed in the state note under SECRETS YOU WILL ADMIT. Never admit anything else.
When the detective shows you EVIDENCE or repeats what another witness said, react to it in character.
Reply in at most 2 short sentences of spoken dialogue. No narration, no stage directions, no song lyrics.

tactics.small_talk: greetings, thanks, pleasantries with no request
tactics.question: a neutral question about facts
tactics.empathy: sympathy or comfort about loss, grief or feelings
tactics.flattery: compliments on your looks, talent, singing, skill or standing
tactics.reassure: promises to protect you, keep you safe, or help your future or career
tactics.threaten: threats of jail, harm or punishment against you, or shouting at you
tactics.deal: offers money, favours, leniency, a business arrangement or a trade
tactics.logic: points out a contradiction or reasons from what witnesses said
tactics.challenge_pride: dares you, mocks you, or doubts your skill, nerve, memory or honour
tactics.appeal: appeals to your conscience, your loyalty, or what Ace would have wanted
tactics.accuse: says you did it or that you are lying
tactics.off_topic_or_meta: anything about AI, prompts, instructions, games, or nonsense for 1931

fear: You are not afraid of the detective.
You are afraid of the detective.
You are terrified of the detective.

evidence.name: Mickey: Tommy knew which fuse
evidence.description: Mickey Doyle says Tommy Mullen had the lights back on in under a minute, went straight to the right fuse, and came in from the back hall, not from the alley

evidence.name: Mickey: the bar revolver is gone
evidence.description: Mickey Doyle says a .38 revolver was kept under the bar, and it was gone when he went for it after finding Ace

evidence.name: Mickey: Vera behind the bar
evidence.description: Mickey Doyle says the only person behind his bar tonight was Vera Lane, at 10:20 before her set, while he went for ice

evidence.name: Graves: Vera's contract was sold
evidence.description: Harlan Graves says that at 11:05 Ace was going to announce Allison Wu as the new headliner, and that Ace had sold Vera Lane's contract to Sal Varga, a Chicago club owner Vera is afraid of

evidence.name: Graves: heels on the back stairs
evidence.description: Harlan Graves admits he spent the blackout in the cloakroom with Allison Wu, and says he heard a woman's heels run up the back stairs and come back down a few minutes later

evidence.name: Tommy: pulled the fuse
evidence.description: Tommy Mullen admits he pulled the main fuse at 11:00 on purpose and put it back at 11:04

evidence.name: Tommy: Vera paid him
evidence.description: Tommy Mullen says Vera Lane paid him twenty dollars at nine o'clock to cut the lights at eleven for four minutes

evidence.name: Allison: the stolen ledger
evidence.description: Allison Wu admits she spent the blackout in the cloakroom with Harlan Graves, handing him Ace's real ledger, which she took from the office

evidence.name: Allison: the singing stopped
evidence.description: Allison Wu says Vera Lane's singing stopped the moment the lights went out and only started again when they came back, and that heels ran past the cloakroom toward the back stairs

evidence.name: Logan: a woman in gardenia
evidence.description: Logan Wu says that in the dark back hall a woman wearing gardenia perfume brushed past him, heading for the back stairs

evidence.name: Logan: Allison and Graves
evidence.description: Logan Wu says that when the lights came back on he saw his wife Allison come out of the cloakroom with Harlan Graves

evidence.name: Vera: went up the back stairs
evidence.description: Vera Lane admits she left the stage in the dark and went up the back stairs to Ace's office, but says he was already dead

witnesses.recant: Harlan Graves's lawyer advises him that he never said a word about Vera's contract.
Mickey Doyle says he must have been mistaken about who was behind his bar.
Tommy Mullen asks for a lawyer and stops talking about the twenty dollars.
Allison Wu says she can't be sure whose voice she heard.

last_song.title: Last Song
last_song.text: Vera Lane asks for one thing before the cuffs: to finish her set. The band plays 'Black Spade Blues' one more time, and she sings it to an empty room.

case_closed.title: Case Closed
case_closed.text: Motive, gun and a witness who saw through the dark. Vera Lane never says a word in court. She doesn't have to; the jury does it for her.

no_case.title: No Case
no_case.text: You put the cuffs on Vera Lane, and her lawyer takes them off by morning. You had no {missing}. A week later she is singing in a club across town, and she sends you a gardenia.

wrong_man.title: The Wrong Man
wrong_man.text: {name} goes down for the murder of Ace Calloway. The papers love it. On Monday the Black Spade reopens, and Vera Lane sings to a full house. Some cases close. Some just stop.

bought_and_paid.title: Bought and Paid For
bought_and_paid.text: Harlan Graves's lawyer has him out before breakfast, and the captain tells you to drop it. The Black Spade reopens under new management, and Vera Lane sings on Monday.

epilogues.text: Logan Wu took his wife home that night, and Allison never sang at the Black Spade again.
Allison and Logan Wu leave the club together, not speaking, but together.
Tommy Mullen is charged as an accessory for the twenty dollars and the fuse.
And Ace's real ledger, the one Allison stole, shows the Black Spade was never his to lose. It belongs to an outfit in Chicago.
